review.reason:
Select candidate 44 without geometry edits. The numbered preview shows three distinct, playable holes within a compact folded routing.

Hole 1: The 574-yard par 5 runs across the lower property from T1 to G1. Its substantial right-side lake creates sustained placement pressure, while two left-side fairway bunkers complicate simply aiming away from water. The fairway retains ample staging space, and the lake does not block the green entrance. Right/back greenside sand rewards a controlled final approach rather than indiscriminate distance chasing.

Hole 2: The dry 305-yard split-fairway par 4 returns from T2 through the upper property toward G2. The visible central tree-and-sand divider gives the alternative lanes a genuine purpose. Conservative placement around it competes with a more direct green attack; the relatively small target and greenside sand constrain that attack. The simulated one-shot reach indicates an opportunity, not guaranteed safety.

Hole 3: The dry 149-yard punchbowl par 3 plays from T3 toward the larger G3. Its separate foreground landing patch, open green entrance and bilateral rear bunkering provide a forgiving distance-control finish. Center-green play offers more margin than attacking the pin.

The long shoreline par 5, short split-route par 4 and compact dry par 3 provide excellent contrast. Against recent publications, the punchbowl repeats, but its much shorter distance and dry setting differ substantially from course 103. The split fairway and return of the uphill-grinder type add sufficient freshness.

Simulated 3/1/1 shots to green and 59/121/44 safe tee options support fair difficulty; the visible landing spaces independently look credible. The 5:3 preview has varied orientations, nearby G1–T2 and G2–T3 connections, selective trees and continuous interior grass rather than isolated parallel strips. This approves the supplied geometry; generated artwork still requires a separate fidelity and natural-green review.
